- Guards a shared resource so that only a single thread at a time can use it.

- A counter that controls how many threads can access a resource at the same time.
- It has no owner: any thread can signal (release) it, not just the one that waited (acquired) on it.
- Waiting decrements the counter and blocks when no permits remain, and signaling increments it.
- Typical uses: limiting access to a pool of resources, or signaling between threads, such as a producer telling a consumer that data is ready.
